thread.title: Foreign Exchange Rates Weekly Preview: Fed’s Data Dependency Makes the Week Ahead an Important one

author: James Elliot
title: Foreign Exchange Rates Weekly Preview: Fed’s Data Dependency Makes the Week Ahead an Important one
text:
Foreign Exchange Rates Weekly Preview: Fed’s Data Dependency Makes The Week Ahead An Important One Foreign Exchange Rates Weekly Preview: Fed’s Data Dependency Makes The Week Ahead An Important One Facebook Stock markets are recovering after last week’s rout.
But data out of the US will be important, especially given the Fed’s insistence to stay data dependent.
Friday’s US jobs report will be a major market mover. To support the markets it need to come in just right; not too good, but not terrible either.
A new week often brings a change in sentiment, and this seems to be the case this week as equities are due for a strong open. Both the UK’s FTSE and the German Dax are due to open around 0.9% higher and US indices are also up from last week’s close. A strong session on Monday could help break the cycle of selling which caused so much market panic last week and set up a reversal higher.
European indices may even outperform now that the ratings agencies have both announced their decisions on Italy’s credit rating. Standard and Poor’s did so last Friday and left the rating unchanged at BBB, two notches above junk, and one above Moody's (who use different nomenclature). The agency did lower their outlook from 'stable' to 'negative', but the surprise rating hold was enough to push yields down by 4bp.
The Euro meanwhile has gained modestly but has at least held the August lows verse the US dollar which has been on a strong rally through October. With the Fed making clear it will remain data dependent, all eyes will be on the major releases this week, culminating in Friday’s all-important US jobs report.
Monday October 29
Like last week, there are no major earnings releases today. Fed Evans speaks today at 1345. Today is also the UK’s budget statement, the surprise part of which is mainly tax changes. British stocks can be affected, particularly in regulated industries. The main items are usually revealed around 1200-1300.
Tuesday October 30
Eurozone GDP is released at 1000, but as the individual countries report beforehand this is unlikely to be surprise or move the markets. DJIA components KO and PFE report before the bell, along with V’s competitor MA, beleaguered giant GE, and car maker FCAU. FB is the final FANG to report, its earnings come after the bell, along with fellow tech companies BIDU, IQ and EBAY. The stock has been hammered recently, but as we have seen, an EPS beat on its own may not be enough for relief.
Wednesday October 31
The last day of the month, Hallowe’en is the end of the six-month summer seasonal cycle, where defensives typically outperform risk industries. There is more action than usual in the Asian session. The BoJ policy rate announcement and press conference is scheduled, and Australian inflation data at 0030 is expected to come in at 0.5%.
ADP at 12:15 estimates 5k more than NFP. As always a large beat or miss can jump the gun on the ‘official’ result on Friday. GM report before the open. It will be interesting to compare the results with FCAU, and see how much steel and aluminum tariffs are mentioned.
Thursday November 1
The new month starts today, and is traditionally the start of the winter six month seasonal cycle (risk stocks outperform). Banks are closed in Spain and Italy for All Saints Day, but not their stock markets. There is a rate decision in CZK, a 25bp hike is expected. Today is the pinnacle of the earnings season, with 491 companies reporting, the most of any day in the season, and of course AAPL, the biggest company in the world reports after the bell. It is likely that the AAPL result will set the tone for the whole market. Note that AAPL do not usually release until about 2130.
Friday November 2
It’s the first Friday of the month so it must be NFP day in the US and Canada, so as always, USDCAD volatility is assured. The US estimate is 190k again, the ‘default’ estimate, well above last month, whereas the Canadian estimate is modest after last month’s blowout result. We have the two NFPs and US Trade Balance at 1230, and the Canadian trade balance an hour later. James Elliot James Elliott is an entrepreneur and an independent trader.
